title: Protocol for determination of phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate levels and localization in Candida glabrata by confocal microscopy
protocol: Reconstitute FYVE-GFP-expressing C. glabrata strain on a CAA plate.
Store the revived strain at 4°C for up to 15 days.
Inoculate and grow the strain in 10 mL CAA medium for 16 hours.
Set up a secondary culture with an initial OD600 of 0.1 in 10 mL CAA medium.
Grow the culture at 30°C for 4 hours to obtain logarithmic-phase cells.
Stain the vacuole with FM 4-64 dye.
Harvest 4–5 OD600 logarithmic-phase cells at 2000 × g at 25°C.
Suspend cells in 100 μL CAA medium containing 16 μM FM 4-64 dye.
Incubate the stained cells at 30°C with continuous agitation at 10 × g for 2 hours.
Wash cells three times with 1 mL CAA medium at 25°C.
Collect washed cells via centrifugation at 2000 × g for 5 minutes.
Grow FM 4-64-labeled cells in 10 mL CAA medium for 2 hours at 30°C.
Wash the cells thrice with 1 mL PBS at 2000 × g for 5 min at 25°C.
Stain the plasma membrane with TMA-DPH dye.
Incubate 4–5 OD600 FM 4-64-labeled cells in 100 μL Tris-HCl buffer containing 0.5 μM TMA-DPH dye at 25°C for 10 min with continuous agitation at 10 × g.
Wash cells three times with chilled 1 mL PBS at 4°C and place on ice.
Suspend cells in 200 μL of chilled PBS and store on ice.
Place 6 μL PBS cell suspension in the middle of the slide.
Gently place an inclined coverslip over the cell suspension, avoiding air bubbles.
Remove excess cells by placing a tissue paper on top of the coverslip.
Seal the edges of the coverslip with nail paint.
Label the slide as S1 (Sample 1) on the left-hand side with a marker.
Wait for 30–60 seconds to let the cells settle down before proceeding with image acquisition.
Image cells using the confocal microscope.
Switch on the microscope system.
Switch on the laser and detector components.
Launch Zen Black software.
Select the objective lens using the 'Locate' option in Zen Black.
Choose appropriate laser lines for imaging.
Configure detectors according to experimental requirements.
Set scanning parameters for image acquisition.
Select the appropriate objective lens under the ‘Locate Menu’ command in Zen Black software.
Adjust laser power and gain using the ‘Channels’ option settings.
Set up detector settings using the ‘Imaging Setup’ option.
Configure scanning parameters and select region of interest using the ‘Acquisition mode’ option.
Choose Plan-Apochromat 63x/1.40 Oil objective lens for imaging.
Use three different laser lines: 405 nm, 488 nm, and 561 nm for FM4-64, GFP, and TMA-DPH respectively.
Select detector settings based on the emission spectrum of fluorophores and dyes.
Set laser power to optimally excite fluorophores and dyes.
Adjust detector gain to minimize signal-to-noise ratio.
Confirm accuracy of adjusted settings.
Set up scanning parameters including scanning mode, scan speed, and pixel size.
Define the region of interest (ROI).
Acquire images at four different pixel sizes: 1204*1204, 512*512, 256*256, and 128*128.
Resolve issues impacting image acquisition and quality before capturing images.
Save acquired images for analysis.
Quantify GFP signal intensity from acquired images.
Open images in Zen Blue software for analysis.
Select the 'Measure' option from the left side menu.
Choose the GFP Channel from the ‘Dimensions’ menu to quantify signal intensity on specific structures.
Draw spline contours around the plasma membrane and vacuole using the ‘Spline contour’ option.
Mark the plasma membrane with a red spline contour.
Mark the vacuole with a pink spline contour for quantification.
Use alternative software such as LAS X, NIS-Elements, or ImageJ/Fiji for image analysis if Zen Blue is not available.
Select the 'spline contour' option from the 'Graphics' menu.
Draw one spline contour close to the cell boundary.
Draw another spline contour enclosing the vacuole for measuring FYVE-GFP signal intensity at the plasma membrane and in the vacuole, respectively.
Copy the same spline contour to the blank space where cells are not present.
Tick off the ‘M’ option within the ‘Graphics’ menu to access information on the area and mean intensity values for the selected GFP channel under the spline contour.
Select the ‘Profile view’ option for the intensity plot data against the distance generated for the fluorophore.
Change the 'X and Y-axis settings' options for the selected profile view.
Generate the profile plot that will provide the spatial distribution and the intensity of fluorescent signals across the line drawn.
